speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's clinic. I understand you have been experiencing headaches and worsening vision over the last three weeks; to begin our assessment, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the pain, and do you notice any specific visual changes like blurriness, halos, or loss of peripheral vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis). The combination of age (69), new headache, and progressive vision loss over three weeks is a medical emergency requiring immediate workup for this condition. I will now request an ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) and CRP levels to confirm the diagnosis.
